relevance_note: The paper reports three probands with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants: "WES identified three novel heterozygous mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene".
method_note: Read the full paper and set every value by hand; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and cut table spans directly from the table lines (row label through the patient's cell), and I checked each cut against the tables. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns, headed 'Patient 1', 'Patient 2', 'Patient 3'. Table 4 continuation rows have an empty patient cell, so treatments in those rows are attributed by row order under each patient label. Table 5 (common SLE risk alleles in other genes: C1QTNF12, SLC29A3, TAOK3, PLD2, ANKRD27, UHRF1BP1, CXorf21, CD58, TRAF3, NCF2, CDKN1B, IFIH1) was NOT recorded: patient labels appear only in the first row of each group and some continuation rows are textually identical between the P1 and P3 groups, so per-person attribution cannot be verified from a span. Relatives: P1's mother has a variant row because Table 1 gives the P1 mutation origin as 'From mother' (her zygosity is not stated); P1's son has phenotypes but no variant row (his genotype is not stated in the text; the pedigree is only in Fig. 2); P3's mother is an asymptomatic carrier ('Her mother was asymptomatic'), and 'asymptomatic' was not converted into excluded checklist items. P2's parents (both tested negative by qPCR) and P3's father (trio WES, result not stated) have no rows: the paper gives them no individual labels or clinical data. Variant-level descriptors (type, cDNA, protein, authors' classification) are repeated on relatives' variant rows; functional assays, done on probands' samples only, are not. age_at_diagnosis holds the age at genetic diagnosis (Table 1); ages at LN diagnosis are 29, 3 and 3 years. Narrative ages ('29-year-old', '3-year-old') describe age at SLE diagnosis, so age at last evaluation is not reported for the probands. Group statements applied to all three probands with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement': IL-6 elevation 'in the three patients' (Fig. 4I legend) and renal involvement 'without renal insufficiency'. Discrepancies (none a true contradiction): Table 1 onset header says years but the P2 cell is '10 month'; P2 immunofluorescence lists C9 in Table 2 but not in the text; P2 had no autoantibodies in her first year and became ANA/dsDNA positive later (recorded as observed, with timing in detail); P3 had no fever or proteinuria during follow-up after treatment (an outcome, not recorded as excluded). Checklist judgments: P1 thrombocytopenia and P1's son's anaemia are not called autoimmune, so cytopenia (autoimmune) is not reported for them; P3 'Bilateral knee effusion' was not mapped to arthritis; P2 'vasculitic rashes' was mapped to vasculitis observed; P1's son's Henoch-Schonlein purpura was not mapped to vasculitis. The table category 'Cardiovascular: No' was not used to exclude vasculitis.
